title: Connect ships as both a desktop application and a web app from one codebase, with the web dev server on port 5173
content:
Connect is described as an open-source **desktop and web** application for document model management — the same codebase produces both, and the README's script list is where that duality is visible:

```bash
pnpm start          # desktop app
pnpm run dev        # web app, then http://localhost:5173
pnpm run make       # package the desktop app for the current platform
pnpm run make:mac | make:linux | make:windows
pnpm run docker:build   # build the image once, to test the production deployment locally
```

Its stated role is a **private editor and contributor tool** for contributors of open organisations, with full control over data ownership, available standalone or in the cloud. Two capabilities define the shell: a navigation menu for adding, synchronising and browsing document drives — shared within an organisation or private to the contributor — and the ability to edit any document model type the organisation selected or defined.

Worth pairing with the deployment picture: the published Connect *image* is plain nginx serving a SPA built at image-build time, so the desktop packaging path above and the container path are genuinely different artefacts from the same source.
